clearedSpotChecks.check: L-840 question 1. Does the spill step before the dependency loop of Emitter::write_to_final_stack_offsets in monad v0.16.5 remove every dependency cycle?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read emitter.cpp:1398-1621 in the cycle 16 copy (sha256 1294ce58, as the unit states). Each element with a stack offset at or below top_index and no AVX register adds one count to the single owner of that offset (1446-1460), so the blocking relation is a function and each node has out-degree at most one. Nodes off a cycle lie upstream of a cycle or of a leaf and drain in the first loop. A tree node's final indices cannot be the offset of a cycle node, because that would give the cycle node a second outgoing edge, so the first loop never overwrites a cycle slot before it is read. In the cycle loop (1564-1608) the value of cycle[k-1] is loaded into yx2 before cycle[k] is stored over cycle[k-1]'s offset. The only other elements whose offsets lie in cycle[k]'s final indices are tree nodes that were already written or AVX elements read from their registers. The first value loaded is cycle.back(), whose offset is a final index of e, and e is written last. The 14-AVX-element bound behind yx1 != yx2 holds. In the jump paths (3500-3513, 3761-3794) the only popped holder that keeps an AVX register through the writer is dest, and an AVX-only dest is first copied to sp_offset_temp_word1 (non_literal_jump_dest_operand). The JUMPI condition is consumed by jumpi_comparison before the writer runs. I also checked that clobbering the registers of written AVX elements and of spill_elem does no harm on the paths that continue. begin_new_block (1016-1028) resets the virtual stack unless keep_stack_in_next_block_ is set. That flag is set only in jumpi_keep_fallthrough_stack (3778-3813), where the writer runs only on the taken branch, after the conditional jump to fallthrough_lbl. The writer emits only mov, vmovaps, vmovd, vmovq, vmovups, vpxor and vpcmpeqd (1833-1840, 1961-1988), and none of these changes the flags that conditional_jmp reads after the writer in jumpi_spill_fallthrough_stack. The recorded sweep outputs agree: perm-0-720.txt and shuffle-1-200.txt show bad_final=0, yx_equal=0, avx_clobbered_before_use=0 and digest 18e601f3245c1db8 on every line I read.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-840 question 2. Is a dependency skipped at the AVX register check (emitter.cpp:1457-1459) ever read later from a register that an earlier write in the loop reassigned?
clearedSpotChecks.note: An AVX element has no outgoing edge, so it is never on a cycle and is written in the first loop. Its register becomes the scratch register yx1 only when the element itself is popped (1484-1487), so the register is not overwritten before the element's own stores at 1515-1522. init_yx1 comes from alloc_avx_reg and no stack element holds it. If a spill was needed, spill_elem was first stored to its new offset (1412-1420) or already had another location. The mined replay summary in out/mined2/aggregate.json shows 0 mismatches over 2,007 transactions under each normal order, and 1382 mismatches with planted fault f3. That shows the replay can detect this class of error.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-812 and L-849. Which Monad release mainnet validators run, from headers, RPC client strings and release records.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/changelog/releases. It lists v0.16.7 as mainnet N/A and testnet 2026-11-19. web3_clientVersion on https://rpc.monad.xyz returned Monad/0.16.7 on 2026-11-25. This matches out/rpc/clientversion.txt, so the mixed fleet the unit describes is real. The version question only matters if the two releases emit different words at block exits. The unit's proof covers both the v0.16.5 map order and the vector order, so the inconclusive outcome for L-849 changes no PoolManager result. The cleared outcome for L-812 depends on the cycle 16 and 17 harnesses for v0.16.7, which I did not rerun.
